tob-10493: The Belgian playwright Maurice Maeterlinck, famous for his symbolist dramas, turns here to quiet essays on the inner life. He writes of silence, of the goodness hidden in simple people, and of a mysterious inner beauty he finds in women and children. These gentle meditations made him one of the most beloved spiritual writers of his generation.
tob-10793: Oxford’s Archibald Sayce compares the religions of the two great river civilizations — Egypt and Babylon — in this scholarly survey. He examines their gods, temples, creation myths, and ideas of the afterlife, drawing on the cuneiform tablets and hieroglyphs then newly deciphered. The book helped found the modern study of ancient Near Eastern religion.
tob-9047-57493: Pliny the Elder’s Natural History is Rome’s great storehouse of lore — seven-and-thirty books on all, from star-lore to beast-lore. tob-4093: Hermann Oldenberg’s volume turns the Grihya-Sutras — old India’s house-rite books, for birth, wedding, and burial. These rules ordered daily life in Vedic days. The rendering opened the homely, everyday side of Hinduism to western scholars for the first time.
the-lord-of-the-sea-pg6993: M. P. Shiel's visionary novel imagines a superman who masters the sea itself — part lost-world adventure, part Nietzschean fantasy of the coming man. arxiv-2605-08793: Optimal transport — the mathematics of reshaping one distribution into another at minimum cost — powers parts of modern machine learning, but solving it at scale is slow. arxiv-2605-09393: Software engineering students meeting LLMs are pushed by motivators and blocked by demotivators. arxiv-2605-09493: Davis complexes are geometric playgrounds built for Coxeter groups, and products of them host lattices with striking rigidity properties. pmc-13454493: Learning from healthcare incidents — rethought through a Safety-II model integrating work-as-imagined, work-as-done, and work-as-experienced. pmc-13402993: Sodium intake and asthma — time to unravel an old mystery of their pathophysiology. Andrea Portacci, Vitaliano Nicola Quaranta, Silvano Dragonieri, and colleagues pose the question. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is asthma. It asks whether salt worsens asthma. An old mystery.
arxiv-2606-16793: Shuangshuang Chen, Han Cheng, and colleagues prove decay estimates for beam equations with potentials in two dimensions. arxiv-2606-17093: Adam Haroon and colleagues fix a subtle failure in fringe projection profilometry, a technique that measures 3D shape by projecting striped light patterns. arxiv-2606-17193: Fred Cohen and Jonathan Pakianathan survey configuration spaces, the spaces of all possible positions of points, and their connection to braid groups. arxiv-2606-17393: R.M. Green and Tianyuan Xu connect perfect matchings, Fano planes, and orthogonal bases of type E8. The exceptional E8 lattice hides combinatorial gems, and the paper links its bases to classical designs. The work is pure mathematical beauty with echoes in coding theory.
plos-pone-0003393: Human geneticists surveyed nature's stop signs in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003493: Sleep researchers quantified a dangerous combination in this 2008 driving study. plos-pone-0003593: Leukemia researchers built a DNA-guided missile in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003693: In 2008, Carling, Kristoffersen, and Herrin asked how doctors should present treatment odds. plos-pone-0003793: Pears, Thornber, and Auger split platelet signaling by isoform in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003893: Back in 2008, a group caught two signals wrestling over one gene switch. In fruit flies, blocking Wg signaling came down to Mad and Armadillo competing for the dTcf binding site. The competition shows developmental pathways settling disputes by molecular tug-of-war.
plos-pone-0003993: In 2009, Fukushima, Nakao, and Shinoe made hippocampus cells more excitable by subtraction. Removing NMDA receptors from CA3 neurons boosted their firing instead of quieting them. plos-pone-0004093: In 2008, El-Hage, Bruce-Keller, and Yakovleva linked drugs and virus in the brain. Morphine worsened HIV-1 Tat-driven cytokine output from star-shaped astrocytes. plos-pone-0004193: In 2009, a team watched young brains rewire. Axon pullback in the silenced visual cortex did not need synapses. Neural pruning ran on experience alone. The finding splits rewiring from synapse rivalry. The work reframes how early vision sculpts the brain.

plos-pone-0004493: In 2009, a team found sleeping sickness's coat extra. Major surface glycoproteins of insect-form Trypanosoma brucei proved nonessential for transmission. The germ's famous coat wasn't needed in flies. The neat finding shifts germ biology. The coats had long been thought vital.
plos-pone-0004593: In 2009, Du, Qian, and Zhu found a Parkinson's drug turning toxic via iron anew. L-DOPA neurotoxicity was mediated by up-regulation of DMT1-IRE expression. The drug boosted brain iron uptake. The finding warns on dosing levels. The toxic mechanism was iron-driven.
plos-pone-0004693: In 2009, Khandoga and a team watched white cells marching to fresh injury anew. Live imaging tracked white cells moving toward fresh injury. The neat test enabled live tracking here. The study maps inflammation wiring anew today. The cell movement is guided well.
plos-pone-0358993: Diabetic macular edema — swelling in the retina caused by diabetes — can steal central vision, and some patients do not respond to standard drugs. plos-pone-0355693: Parents admitted to psychiatric wards are separated from their children — at the worst possible moment. plos-pone-0358593: Tuberculosis can spike blood sugar even in people who never had diabetes — and that may worsen their outcome. plos-pone-0357793: Celebrity homes converted into museums must satisfy real visitors, not just admirers. plos-pone-0357593: Treating PTSD inside virtual reality could make therapy more powerful and accessible. plos-pone-0356693: Learning human anatomy pits digital resources against flipped classrooms. plos-pone-0353293: Potentially toxic elements hide in the surface soils of townships across northwest Hebei. This paper identified their sources and assessed the health risks. The source-to-risk assessment gives local authorities the evidence to protect residents.
plos-pone-0357093: A blue pigment from spirulina — phycocyanobilin — may calm the immune chaos of lupus. plos-pone-0355293: Waterlogging rewrites plant biochemistry — including the fatty acids in their tissues. plos-pone-0356793: Iron deficiency stalks infants in the high Andes, where thin air already strains young bodies. plos-pone-0355393: Multidrug-resistant gut bacteria stack resistance genes like armor plating. plos-pone-0356493: Long-acting contraceptives could transform rural Bangladeshi women’s lives — yet uptake stays stubbornly low. plos-pone-0356393: Cognitive impairment among older Palestinians — in communities and nursing homes — was poorly measured until now. This paper established its prevalence in both settings. plos-pone-0353193: Bempedoic acid — a newer cholesterol drug — must prove its worth in cost as well as efficacy. plos-pone-0356293: British young people’s moods shift with the seasons — measurably. plos-pone-0345893: Ancient Ge’ez manuscripts in an Ethiopian church — irreplaceable heritage — face decay. plos-pone-0354593: Long COVID impairs balance and trunk control in ways patients feel but doctors struggle to measure. plos-pone-0354293: Predicting how liposomes release their drug cargo usually demands tedious lab work. This paper predicted in vitro liposome release profiles using explainable machine learning. plos-pone-0355493: Pigs’ carbon footprint varies across production stages — and quantifying it is the first step to shrinking it. plos-pone-0354893: Barbell back squat technique — bar position, stance width, reps, load — changes which muscles work hardest. This paper measured muscle activity across those variables. The findings give lifters and coaches the biomechanical evidence to program squats for specific strength goals.
plos-pone-0355193: Can personality traits predict self-reported binary gender — and do machines agree with classic statistics? plos-pone-0354793: Mandarin verb-direction constructions — V+xia, V+xialai, V+xiaqu — encode subtle directional meanings. This quantitative comparative study dissected them. plos-pone-0353693: Processed colostrum — from a spring-calving dairy herd — its bacterial and archaeal microbiota characterized. This paper did so. plos-pone-0353393: Biodiversity patterns in an island archipelago hotspot — shaped by sampling bias and uneven coverage. This paper demonstrated it. plos-pone-0353993: Chemsex among men who have sex with men in Yangon — prevalence, practices, and risk factors. This paper documented them. The findings revealed drug-sex intersections in Myanmar. The research informed harm reduction — meeting a hidden population where it actually is.
plos-pone-0352793: 3D point clouds — classified and segmented by efficient long-range modeling. This paper built that lightweight architecture. The model captured distant dependencies without heavy computation. The findings advanced 3D vision — machines understanding space, efficiently.
plos-pone-0349693: Resuscitation training for healthcare professionals — its evidence syntheses mapped and appraised. This systematic review of reviews protocol outlines the work. plos-pone-0352693: Fragile X syndrome mice — Fmr1 loss reorganizing multi-elemental composition across tissues. This paper demonstrated it. plos-pone-0343793: Old World Swallowtail butterflies — evolution across the Palearctic revealed by integrative analyses. This paper did so. The findings traced the butterfly’s continental history. plos-pone-0352893: Lignin-formaldehyde resin — lab-scale prototype of a bio-renewable wood adhesive. This paper developed it. The findings replaced petroleum with plant waste. plos-pone-0352993: Soccer post-activation performance enhancement — conditioning activities after sport-specific warm-up. This paper tested them. The findings identified the best primers. plos-pone-0352593: Electroretinography as a cognitive impairment biomarker — a scoping review protocol for non-invasive early detection in elders. This paper outlines it. plos-pone-0352193: Sugarcane cultivation — meat waste-derived organic fertilizer integrated with chemical fertilizer. This paper tested the application. plos-pone-0351693: Coronavirus spike genes — genus- and host-associated codon usage bias patterns. This paper characterized them. The analysis read the synonymous choices across coronaviruses. plos-pone-0351293: Japanese acute tocolysis — trends and determinants from 2012 to 2023 in an 11-year nationwide cohort. This paper studied them. The analysis tracked the labor-stalling practice. europmc-pmc2817393: When cells are stressed, they can eat their own damaged parts for survival, a process called autophagy. europmc-pmc2820493: Predicting how drug candidates fit into protein targets is central to drug design. europmc-pmc2848993: The immune system's HLA genes need precise naming to avoid chaos in transplantation. This 2010 paper presents the official nomenclature for factors of the HLA system. europmc-pmc2885493: Body inflammation can slow the mind's engine. This 2008 paper links peripheral inflammation to altered substantia nigra activity and slower movement in humans. europmc-pmc2909393: Rare microbes hide in sequencing data as a blurry rare biosphere. This 2010 paper sharpens the picture with better OTU clustering of similar sequences. The authors' method irons out the wrinkles in grouping. Their fix made rare-microbe surveys far more trustworthy.
europmc-pmc2939793: Cancer might be smelled on the breath. This 2010 paper detects lung, breast, bowel, and prostate cancers from exhaled breath with a nanosensor array. europmc-pmc2964293: A workhorse mosquito cell line has a broken antiviral defense. This 2010 paper shows C6/36 Aedes albopictus cells carry a broken RNA interference response against viruses. europmc-pmc3004893: A probiotic strain tightens the gut wall. This 2010 paper shows Lactobacillus plantarum MB452 boosts gut-seal genes and strengthens the barrier. The authors reveal the tightening. europmc-pmc3018493: Manganese in well water may dull young minds. This 2011 paper links manganese in drinking water to lower IQ in schoolchildren. The authors warn well users. Their work shaped water standards. Quebec wells carried the highest loads. Filters now strip the metal cheaply.
europmc-pmc3027093: Poor countries need smart health staffing. This 2011 review surveys who does what in low-income clinics, from doctors to aides. The authors weigh task-shifting evidence. europmc-pmc3027693: Blue-tinted light keeps us alert. This 2011 study tests whether blue-rich light boosts alertness and thinking. The authors find it beats dim warm light. Their work informs office lighting. Night-shift nurses may benefit most. The effect runs through the eyes' hidden sensors.
europmc-pmc3040193: Human blood got a chemical census. This 2011 paper lists the thousands of small molecules floating in human serum. The authors' catalog powers marker hunts. Their resource is free to all. Doctors compare patients against this baseline. The census keeps growing with new tools.
europmc-pmc3145793: Wilt pathogens' niches got compared. This 2011 paper uses comparative genomics to study vascular wilt pathogens' adaptations. The authors reveal niche tricks. europmc-pmc3386193: Colon cancer germs got mapped. This 2012 paper maps gut germs in colorectal cancer patients. The authors reveal the shifts. Their work guides screening. Chen's team led the work. The paper is widely cited. It shaped stool-test research. The study is a classic.

europmc-pmc3407993: Wine, beer, and plant compounds got a heart review. This 2012 paper reviews alcohol and polyphenols in heart disease and cancer. The authors weigh the evidence. Their overview guides nutrition. Arranz's review is widely cited. Moderation won, they found. It is a classic.
europmc-pmc6515593: Tumors recruit macrophages - immune cells meant to eat invaders - and reprogram them into bodyguards that shield the cancer. europmc-pmc6516193: Fat tissue in obesity fills with worn-out senescent cells that leak inflammatory signals and worsen diabetes. europmc-pmc6651993: Why does anti-PD-1 immunotherapy work wonders in some liver cancers and flop in others? europmc-pmc6758693: Medical schools moved classes online - but does the screen teach as well as the ward? This systematic review compared online versus offline learning in undergraduate medical education. The verdict guides educators balancing convenience against the hands-on craft of doctoring.
